one_month_reasoning: No earnings fall in the window: Q3 FY27 results come in early December, after 2026-10-30. The CEO shock (Desai gave notice Sep 24; the exit to Meta was announced Sep 28) is already in the price. The stock went from $410 to an intraday low near $300 and back to $356 on the investor day, reaffirmed Q3/FY27 guidance and the $1.0B buyback addition ($1.354B now remaining). The FOMC meets Oct 27-28. In round 1 I used Polymarket's ~67% hike odds from Sep 26. That is stale: after the cooler Sep 30 PCE print (core 3.3% y/y), swaps price about 36% (Bloomberg via supervisor), and the $356 close already reflects this. So the FOMC is closer to a two-sided event than a headwind, which slightly reduces my small downside skew. Unscheduled risks run both ways: naming a permanent CEO (upside) or further executive departures (downside). The rebound from the sharp gap-down could run further, but CEO-turnover studies show higher volatility and no reliable drift. Net: median ~$357, with sigma ~17.5% for the month (annual vol/3.5 = 20%, trimmed because no earnings print falls in the window). The ladder is essentially symmetric in log terms around today's price.

fair_value.method: Blend of EV/NTM sales (8x on ~$4.15B NTM revenue at Sept 2027 (1/3 FY28 + 2/3 FY29) plus ~$2.6B net cash over ~85M shares = ~$421), P/E (40x ~$9.9 NTM non-GAAP EPS = ~$396) and FCF yield (32x ~$0.95B FY29 FCF plus cash = ~$388), weighted 40/35/25 = ~$404. I round down to $402 for the March FY28 guide risk, which the multiples do not fully capture.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: NTM revenue at 2027-09-30 ~$4.15B (1/3 FY28 $3.64B + 2/3 FY29 $4.40B) x 8.0x = $33.2B EV + ~$2.6B net cash = $35.8B / ~85M fully diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Reaffirmed on Sep 28 alongside the CEO transition.

The Investor Day target is 20%+ total growth over ~3 years (prior target high teens) with Atlas mid-20s. Q2 grew 30% and beat the Q2 guide by ~5%. Offsetting that, the FY27 guide implies Q4 only +14-16% against $695.1M. I use 21%: FY28 $3.64B, FY29 $4.40B.
The fiscal year ends Jan 31, so Oct-2027 to Sep-2028 covers ~4 months of FY28 and ~8 of FY29 (supervisor correction).

Today's EV (~$28B) over NTM revenue (~$3.35B) is ~8.4x. The trailing EV/sales history has a median of ~12x and a low of ~10x. I hold slightly below today's level because rates are restrictive (10Y ~5.2%) and SBC is ~20% of revenue.
$2.41B cash and ST investments at 7/31/26, no debt. I add ~$0.7B of FCF and subtract ~$0.5B of buybacks, which hold the share count flat.
85.8M non-GAAP fully diluted in Q2. Buybacks from the $1.354B remaining authorization offset SBC dilution.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM non-GAAP EPS at Sept 2027 ~$9.9 x 40x

inputs_detail.input: FY27 non-GAAP op income and EPS guide

inputs_detail.derivation: 21% growth plus 150bp/yr of margin expansion (deck: 100-200bp) takes op income from $626M (20.8%) to FY28 ~$812M and FY29 ~$1,047M. Net income is ~0.89x op income (20% LT tax rate plus interest income) over ~86M shares, giving FY28 ~$8.4 and FY29 ~$10.8. Weighted 1/3 and 2/3, that is ~$10.0; I round down to $9.9. My round-1 $9.0 used ~22% EPS growth and missed the margin leverage.

~49x NTM today. I compress it to 40x (from 42x in round 1) because SBC is ~20% of revenue and GAAP EPS is only $0.53-0.77. I trim the multiple rather than the EPS so the leadership and rate risk is counted only once.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY29 FCF ~$0.95B x 32x (3.1% yield) = $30.4B + $2.6B net cash / 85M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Investor Day deck. '>$1B FY30 FCF' is not stated in the deck; it is only derived from the targets.
~90% conversion on ~$1.05B FY29 non-GAAP op income (see the P/E leg).
A 3.1% yield for a ~20% grower with heavy SBC, with the 10Y at ~5.2%.

bear.story: The March 2027 FY28 guide confirms the deceleration the FY27 guide implies for Q4 (+14-16%), and the reset repeats the last two March prints (-27% in 2025, -22% in 2026). The CEO search drags, Postgres/DocumentDB pressure shows up in Atlas, and the stock trades at ~5-6x NTM sales.

base.story: MDB keeps its ~5% beat habit, so H2 runs ~18-25% and FY28 is guided near 20%. Margins expand ~150bp and a credible permanent CEO is named. The multiple is roughly flat, so the price tracks ~$9.9 NTM EPS at ~40x.

bull.story: AI and agent workloads keep Atlas near 28-30%, the FY28 guide lands above 20%, the $1.35B buyback shrinks the count modestly, and the multiple re-rates toward the ~10-12x historical EV/sales median. That is consistent with street-high targets of $525-565.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$240 (-33%, the $216-250 region of the 2026 selloff lows), the market would be pricing Atlas growth in the mid-teens, a failed leadership transition or a FY28 guide well below 20%, not ordinary 70%-vol noise. That is ~5.3x NTM sales on ~$4.15B, a level MDB has reached only on genuine fundamental or macro breaks (2022 -65%, 2025 -51%).

catalysts.event: FOMC decision; hike odds ~36% after the Sep 30 PCE (down from ~67% on Polymarket before the print)
Permanent CEO named (search firm retained; Ittycheria interim, also a Sequoia partner)
Q3 FY27 earnings; guide $756-761M (+20-21%) and $1.57-1.61 EPS; the Q2 guide was beaten by ~5%
Q4 FY27 results and first FY28 guide. The FY27 guide implies Q4 at only +14-16%; March prints moved the stock -27% (2025) and -22% (2026)
Q2 FY28 earnings, the last print before the horizon
Execution of the $1.354B remaining buyback authorization (~4.6% of market cap)

key_uncertainties: The March 2027 FY28 guide: does MDB guide near 20% or reset again, as the implied Q4 (+14-16%) hints?
Who becomes permanent CEO, and whether sales leadership holds after two CEO changes in ~11 months
Whether Atlas holds ~27-30% growth or slows toward the mid-20s target
Rates: the 10Y is ~5.2% and the Fed is in a hiking cycle, though October hike odds fell to ~36% after PCE
Postgres/DocumentDB competition as a cap on the multiple; no sign of it in reported numbers yet
Macro: Kalshi prices a 2027 recession at ~20-24%, and consumption revenue is cyclical
reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor fixed three errors in my round 1. (1) NTM EPS: the NTM window at Sep 2027 is 1/3 FY28 + 2/3 FY29, and margin expansion lifts op-income growth to ~28%/yr. I rebuilt it from the $626M FY27 op-income guide and get ~$10.0, rounded to $9.9 (was $9.0). (2) Buyback: $1.354B remains out of a $2.0B aggregate authorization, not $2B, so buybacks roughly offset SBC and do not shrink the count. (3) October hike odds: ~36% after the Sep 30 PCE, not 67%. I confirmed that the Polymarket prints of 65-67% predate the PCE release, so my macro drag was overstated. Rates are still restrictive (10Y ~5.2%), so I keep 8x EV/sales and cut the P/E from 42x to 40x for SBC. The corrected fair value is ~$402 (was $390). Base-rate work, which I checked against the March releases: the first-guide March print is MDB's highest-risk event. In 2024 the FY25 guide absorbed an $80M headwind and the stock fell; March 2025 fell ~27% and March 2026 ~22% (after a beat, on implied deceleration). The FY27 guide implies Q4 at +14-16% against a +27% comparison. I weigh that against MDB's ~5% beat habit (Q2 $771.8M vs a $734M high end) and put a slightly heavier bear weight (26%) on it. Scenarios (230/26%, 400/49%, 550/25%) give a mean of ~$393. The ladder uses a lognormal with a ~$377 median and sigma ~0.55 (below the 71% realized vol, which is inflated by the CEO shock), with thinned extreme tails. Compared with round 1, it is 0.5-1pt higher through the middle, from better earnings power, partly offset by the March-guide risk. Research this round was limited to 2 searches.
